## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

The map (`explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:441-456`, "B.12 Native code and Java interop") puts walk's binding of a helper in `StaticNativeApp`, which is where a declared type gets its Java carrier (F-299); P-58 gives the binding's form; P-164 gives the shape. The precedent is rung W's writer side, which repaired the same kind of site in `Writer.fss`, both of its objects (`Writer`, `BufferedWriter`); its file has no other site. The sites of the same kind left in the one library: in `File.fss` two (`FileReadStream`, `FileWriteStream`) and in `Reader.fss` one (`Reader`, with `stdIn`), all three repaired here; after this change no I/O object names a glue class, and the native components left are `FlatString`, `Reflect`, `AnyType`, `FortressBuiltin` and `NativeArray` (`grep -ln '^native component' Library/*.fss ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/*.fss`).

The ways the language and the library offer, and the choice:

- A Java-backed value in a field of a plain object, as P-164 takes: chosen, as `Writer` and the team's `BirdyLib` `FileReadStream` do.
- The object keeps one value parameter and fills a field from the name, as `BirdyLib` does (`jbr: JavaBufferedReader = makeJavaBufferedReader(filename)`): then `stdIn` would need an object of its own, since its reader is not opened by a name (fork W2's reasoning in rung W; R7 takes the two-parameter header).
- Each method a `builtinPrimitive` in the object itself, over a helper that takes the object: not taken, since no Java type carries a program object (`interpreter.md`, "Natives") and P-164 puts the natives on the trait.
- The end's -1 by a fourth new helper beside `jbrRead`: not taken (fork R1); by `read(): ZZ32`: not taken, it leaves the prelude's method.
- `FileWriteStream`'s `write(s: String)` as `Writer`'s, `under.write(s)` then `under.flush()`, or inheriting `WriteStream`'s `writes`, `print` and `println`, which flush after each: not taken; the team's own text of `FileWriteStream` already writes through `writeOn` and only lacked `WriteStream` and `flush` (rows 900, 901), so the change keeps its lines and their buffering.

## 1. What changed and why

The change:

- `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/useful/PartialOrder.scala`, new, 85 lines: `class PartialOrder[T](xs: List[T], lt: (T, T) => Boolean)`. It reads `lt` at most once for each ordered pair, through a memo of n² bytes (`:21-23`, `:26-37`). An element is never compared with itself, and two places of `xs` that hold one object are not each other's predecessors (`:27`), as the base's `!(d eq c)` read them. `minimal` (`:48-50`) holds the elements that no other element precedes, in `xs`'s order, reading the pairs in the base's `minimal`'s order. `linear` (`:52-84`) is a linear extension: round by round, the first element of `xs` that no element left precedes; where every element left has one, as on a cycle, the first left (`:78`). Each element keeps the predecessor it was last found blocked by, so a later round reads on from it rather than from the start (`:55-68`); this changes which reads are repeated from the memo, never their answers.
- `Functionals.scala:718`: `minimal` over the class.
- `Functionals.scala:728-733`: `callType` takes the head of `minimal`, or `cs.head` where it is empty, and sorts nothing (fork K3); the tie type reads the same `minimal`.
- `Functionals.scala:764-768` and `:783`: one `PartialOrder` over the candidates gives `sorted` (`linear`) and `top` (`minimal`), so the two share its memo. The tie at `:831-836` keeps `sorted.headOption`, now the first minimal candidate in the candidates' order (fork K2).
- `CoercionOracle.scala:240-259`: the coercion's candidates in the class's linear extension, by `moreSpecificCandidate(c1, c2)(this)` as before.
- `Formula.scala:610`: the ancestors in the class's linear extension, by `isTrue(ta.subtype(b, a))` as before.
- Each of the three files imports the class (`Functionals.scala:28`, `CoercionOracle.scala:32`, `Formula.scala:31`), so every line below an import moves down by one.
- `PartialOrderJUTest.scala`, new, 56 lines: the class's contract on divisibility over 2 to 65 shuffled (a linear extension in `xs`'s order where nothing else decides, `minimal` against the base's formula, every ordered pair read once), a cycle, one object twice (no read), and the empty list.

- problem: the code generator stops, 'Not in the trait table: OpenRange', at 8 declarations of RangeInternals under the switch-over's setting (F-34; `explorations/perf-probes/codegen-distance/REPORT.md`, section 3), and on the base at row 733's form, in `dumpMethodChaining` (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-28/PROBES.md:115-124`, probe 4); row 733, `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:892`
- spec: `Specification/basic/traits.tex`, "Method Declarations", row 733's citation: an object has the methods that its supertraits provide; the explicit import of a functional method's name, `Specification/basic/components/source-code.tex:172-200`
- precedent: `STypesUtil.gatherMethods` names the trait of each supertrait's declarations as an extends clause names it (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/useful/STypesUtil.scala:1647`, through `mapOverAllSupertraits`, `:1299`); the team's commented-out form beside the edited line, `inheritedMethods` over the extends entry, names each entry so too (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:940`, `STypesUtil.scala:1387-1527`)
- deviation: the first supertrait's own declarations are found by the identity of the index's method objects, not by a name, since a name's `equals` compares its span (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes/Id.java:54-72`); the entry keeps the static arguments and the replacer that `allMethods` gives it, and only its trait's name changes (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:1024-1059`)
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:941`

## 1. What changed, and why

`dumpMethodChaining` (`CodeGen.java:916-1022`) gives an object a forwarder for each method body that it inherits from a supertrait other than the first, unless the first supertrait already brings that method through the class hierarchy. To know that, it compares the trait of each same-named method of the first supertrait with the trait of the body (`typeAnalyzer.equiv`, `:1010`). It took the first supertrait's methods from `STypesUtil.allMethods` (`:941` on the base).

`allMethods` makes its tuples in `gatherMethods` (`STypesUtil.scala:1640-1658`). A supertrait's declarations get the trait as an extends clause names it (`:1647`, the key that `mapOverAllSupertraits` puts at `:1299`). The trait's own declarations get the name that the trait's declaration gives itself (`:1651`, `ti.ast.getHeader.getName`, made into a type at `:1748-1750`). For a trait of an imported api, that is the name in the api's file, with no api name: the probe's message gives the span of the api's header, `C @ ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/TraitTableApiTraitApi.fsi:4:7`.

The code generator's trait table is made over the component and the api environment (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/CodeGenerationPhase.java:179`, `:206-210`). It finds a name without an api in the component, else in four prelude apis only, `CompilerBuiltin`, `CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerAlgebra` and `GeneratorLibrary` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TraitTable.scala:72-101`, "A terrible search hack"). So `equiv` asks `typeCons` for `C`, which throws (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:884`).

The edit (`CodeGen.java:941`, `:1024-1059`): `dumpMethodChaining` reads the first supertrait's methods through a new private method, `firstSupertraitMethods`. It takes `allMethods`' relation, finds the first supertrait's index in the table by the extends clause's name, and gives each tuple whose method is one of that index's own declarations (dotted, functional, getters and setters, by identity) the trait as the extends clause names it, with the tuple's own static arguments. Every other tuple stays as `allMethods` gives it. For a local first supertrait both names find the same index, so the comparison's answer does not change for a program that compiled before.

## 2. Where the fix is, the type that the comparison read, and why the table did not find it

- Where: `CodeGen.java:941` and the new `firstSupertraitMethods`, `:1024-1059`, both inside the code generator; no checker code changes (fork T1).
- The type read: `alreadyType = str.replaceIn(tupAlready._3())` (`CodeGen.java:1009`), the trait of a tuple of the first supertrait's own declarations, `TraitType` `C` without its api, made at `STypesUtil.scala:1748-1750` from the api's header name (`:1651`).
- Why the table did not find it: the table over the component looks up a name without an api in the component and in the four prelude apis only (`TraitTable.scala:72-101`), and the trait is declared in the program's own api.

## 3. The tests

New tests, each named by its topic:

- `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/TraitTableApiTraitCompiled.fss` and `.test` (`tests=`, `compile`, `link`, `run`, `run_out_contains=PASS`), with its api `TraitTableApiTraitApi.fsi` and its component `TraitTableApiTraitApi.fss`, in the form of `RecursiveApiTest3.test`. The api's `trait C abstract tag(self, n: ZZ32): String end` and the generic `trait G[\T\] abstract gtag(self, n: ZZ32): String end`; the program's `trait D tag(self, s: String): String = s end`, `object O extends { C, D } tag(self, n: ZZ32): String = "c" end`, `trait E gtag(self, s: String): String = s end` and `object P extends { G[\(ZZ32, ZZ32)\], E } gtag(self, n: ZZ32): String = "g" end`, with eight assertions: each body through the object and through a value of each supertrait's type.

result.reportText:
# Rung H, `rung-runtime-threads`: the run time's own threads, `abort` and the task trace on compiled helpers

- problem: six bindings of the one library named walk's glue classes, so a compiled body would fall through to the library's own `builtinPrimitive`, which fails: `Thread`'s `val`, `wait`, `ready` and `stop` and the top-level `abort` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:775-786` at 157323e5) and `printTaskTrace` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4625` at 157323e5); F-32, "The compiled path cannot reuse walk's glue classes", counts them among its 102.
- spec: `Specification/advanced/parallelism-locality/transactions.tex:15-21` (`abort` abandons the innermost `atomic` expression, rolls back its changes and runs it again; outside one it has no effect); `Specification/basic-lib/thread.tex:35-58` (`val`, `wait`, `ready`, `stop`); `Specification/basic/expressions/spawn.tex:21-27`. No chapter names `printTaskTrace`: `grep -rn printTaskTrace Specification/` prints nothing.
- precedent: P-167's device, walk's loader table (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java:47-53` at 157323e5, `stringOps.typeName` to `ObjectPrims$ClassName`); the team's helper class over the compiled run time (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/runtime.java:15-18` at 157323e5); P-162's pair, a read at `T` through `cast` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2643`).
- deviation: the abort tests count their tries by a deadline on the clock, not by a variable, since `abort` rolls such a variable back (decision 7); `printTaskTrace` reads a task's package-private `parent` by reflection, since the brief keeps `runtimeSystem/` out of reach (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/runtime.java:71-90`); `Utility.makeFortressException(name, msg)` is repaired, a file the brief does not name (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/Utility.java:30`); the compiled trace prints `Task: <class>` lines, which no source of the team specifies (`runtime.java:41-48`).
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/runtime.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/Utility.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss`.

Base 157323e5. Commits on `wip/rung-runtime-threads`: 5dba0d1c, the tests; 180751e1, the edit and the raise test. Every stage, suite, ladder run and demo below ran on 180751e1, after its build; no code changed after it.

## 1. What changed and why

**The six helpers** (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/runtime.java`, fork H1), in the team's class beside `loopChunk` and `numThreads`, each with a signature that maps to Fortress:

    public static void abort()                                                   // :34-37
    public static void printTaskTrace()                                          // :41-48
    public static fortress.AnyType.Any threadVal(fortress.AnyType.Any self)      // :52-54
    public static void threadWait(fortress.AnyType.Any self)                     // :56-58
    public static boolean threadReady(fortress.AnyType.Any self)                 // :60-62
    public static void threadStop(fortress.AnyType.Any self)                     // :64-66

- `abort()` throws the compiled `runtimeSystem.TransactionAbortException` when the current thread is a `FortressTaskRunner` and `BaseTask.inATransaction()` holds, and else returns (fork H3). The compiled `atomic` catches that exception, cleans up and runs the block again (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:1737-1765`); the transaction keeps its writes until it commits (`runtimeSystem/Transaction.java`, `TXWrite` and `TXCommit`), so the aborted try's writes vanish.
- `printTaskTrace()` builds the compiled task chain, from `BaseTask.getCurrentTask()` through each task's `parent` (`runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:46`) to the primordial task, the component's own class, one line `Task: <JVM class name>` a task, and writes it with one `print`, so that two chains printed by parallel tasks do not interleave line by line.
- `threadVal`, `threadWait`, `threadReady` and `threadStop` throw `Utility.makeFortressException("fortress.CompilerLibrary$FailCalled", "spawn is not compiled yet")` (fork H2), until the code generator compiles `spawn` (row 82).
- A nested class `runtime.TaskParent` holds the reflective read of `parent`; the wrapper generator wraps every method of a helper class, the private ones too (`compiler/nativeInterface/FortressMethodAdapter.java:215-229` has no access test), so a method over `java.lang.reflect.Field` in `runtime` itself would fail every import of the class.

**The bindings.** `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:775-787`:

    object Thread[\T\] (fcn:()->T)
        val():T         = cast[\T\](valAny())
        private valAny():Any =
            builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.runtime.threadVal")
        wait():()       =
            builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.runtime.threadWait")
        ready():Boolean =
            builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.runtime.threadReady")
        stop():()       =
            builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.runtime.threadStop")
    end

    abort():() = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.runtime.abort")

and `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4625`, `printTaskTrace():() = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.runtime.printTaskTrace")`. `val` is P-162's pair: the compiled rewrite checks a binding against the helper's Java signature (F-298), and a helper answers `Object`, so `val(): T` is `cast[\T\]` over a bare binding at `Any`, which is private, since the api (`FortressBuiltin.fsi:306-313`) does not declare it and does not change. Walk instantiates `spawn`'s `Thread` at `Any` (`interpreter/rewrite/DesugarerVisitor.java:1017-1024`), so its `cast` is `cast[\Any\]`.

**Walk's table** (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java:53-65`, fork H4): six entries in `OWN_OPERATIONS`, each helper's name to today's glue:

| helper | glue |
|---|---|
| `nativeHelpers.runtime.threadVal` | `glue.prim.Thread$val` |
| `nativeHelpers.runtime.threadWait` | `glue.prim.Thread$wait` |
| `nativeHelpers.runtime.threadReady` | `glue.prim.Thread$ready` |
| `nativeHelpers.runtime.threadStop` | `glue.prim.Thread$stop` |
| `nativeHelpers.runtime.abort` | `glue.prim.Thread$abort` |
| `nativeHelpers.runtime.printTaskTrace` | `glue.prim.StringPrim$PrintTaskTrace` |

So walk never loads the six helpers; its `spawn`, transactions and trace run as before, and its `Thread` constructor stays glue.

**`Utility.makeFortressException(name, msg)`** (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/Utility.java:30`). It looked up the exception's constructor over `java.lang.String`, but every compiled exception that takes a message takes the prelude's `String` (`javap` of `fortress.CompilerLibrary$FailCalled`: `public fortress.CompilerLibrary$FailCalled(fortress.CompilerBuiltin$String);`), and the method already passes an `FJavaString`, a `CompilerBuiltin.String`. So every compiled helper raise with a message ended in `FortressImplementationError`, which no `catch` sees: the 13 raises with a message in `nativeHelpers/fileOps.java` (2), `compiler/runtimeValues/FortressBufferedReader.java` (6) and `FortressBufferedWriter.java` (5), twelve of them `makeFortressException(name, e)` and one `(name, msg)` (`FortressBufferedReader.java:120`), and the four raises of fork H2. The lookup now names `fortress.CompilerBuiltin.String.class`, one token. Under walk nothing changes: no compiled exception class is on walk's class path (the bootstrap stubs in `ProjectFortress/build/fortress/` hold no exception), so `Class.forName` still fails first and `StaticNativeApp.raised` (`interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:277-282`) still raises the library's object by name.

## 2. The tests

- `ProjectFortress/tests/RuntimeOwnOperationsWalk.fss`, a guard: a spawned thread's `wait`, `ready`, `val` and `stop`; `abort()` outside `atomic`, after which the next line runs; `abort()` inside `atomic` on every try that starts before a deadline 20 ms ahead, with a write before it and one after it, so that the block commits once with only its first write (`x = 10`) and at or after the deadline; `printTaskTrace()` inside a spawned thread, whose `val` still answers.
- `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/RuntimeOwnOperationsCompiled.fss` and `.test`: `runtime.abort`, `runtime.printTaskTrace`, `runtime.threadVal` and `simpleLongArith.longNanoTime` bound in the test's own declarations; `abortC()` outside `atomic`, and inside one as in the walk test; `traceC()` in each iteration of `for i <- 0#4`, whose second half runs in the prelude's loop task; `valC(Handle)` caught as `FailCalled`. Its key `run_out_matches=(?s).*Task: [^\n]*task[0-9]+\nTask: RuntimeOwnOperationsCompiled\n.*PASS.*` asserts a trace whose first line names a generated task class and whose next line names the primordial task, the component itself, and `PASS`.
- `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/HelperRaiseMessageCompiled.fss` and `.test`: the prelude's `makeJavaBufferedReader` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:1173`, over `fileOps.jbrOpen`) on a missing file, caught as `FileNotFoundException`.

## 3. Where the fix belongs, and the precedent

- The place: `explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md`'s rows for `spawn` and `atomic` put walk's half in `glue/prim/Thread.java` and `evaluator/tasks/`, and the compiled transactions in `runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java`; the natives' strings are read in `interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java`, `checkAndLoadNative`. <!-- Report of climb batch 28's rung S, rung-system-natives: System's getEnvironment and getProperty onto stringOps, and args built in Fortress over two scalar helpers of a new class programArgs (review-queue item 355, option 1; row 895; Q3, option 1; P-170). -->

# Rung S: System's natives off systemOps, and args over two scalar helpers

- **problem:** against the one library the checker cannot read `System`: 'FortressBuiltin.StringVector is undefined.', 'File System.fss has 1 error.' (`explorations/compile-ladder/plan-28/PROBES.md:93-97`; F-321; row 895), and `args` reads a glue class with no compiled analogue (`Library/System.fss:29-35` at the base; F-32).
- **spec:** none. `grep -rln "getEnvironment\|getProperty\|programName" Specification/` prints only `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, and `grep -rn "\bSystem\b" Specification/basic-lib Specification/basic Specification/library` prints no api `System`; the only `args` passages are the old `run(args)` parameter (`Specification/preliminaries/overview.tex:71-80`).
- **precedent:** `stringOps.lineSeparator`, the binding that climb batch 26's rung T moved off `systemOps` for the same refusal (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/stringOps.java:75-78`; `Library/FlatString.fss:25-26`); `systemOps.getArgs`, the team's helper over the compiled main's arguments (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/systemOps.java:24-26`); the library's immutable-array factory and `tabulate` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2371-2372`, `:2576`); a private binding in a component (`Library/FlatString.fss:25-26`).
- **deviation:** `programArgs` holds no static of its own: `count` and `at` read `MainWrapper.cachedArgs` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/programArgs.java:9-17`), which the compiled main already sets (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/MainWrapper.java:67`) and walk's driver now sets (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/StringPrim.java:124`), so `MainWrapper.java` is not edited, against fork S3's letter (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-28.md:440`); `count` answers 0 where no entry set the arguments (`programArgs.java:11`); `args` is fork S4's expression over two lines (`Library/System.fss:29-30`).
- **historical:** `Library/System.fss`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/StringPrim.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/systemOps.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/stringOps.java`, each present at the team's last commit `a874948ac` (`gh api "repos/palimondo/fortress/contents/<path>?ref=a874948ac"` answers a blob for each; `StringPrim.java`'s, `c3446329`, is the base's). Commit `ee14222d`'s message calls `stringOps.java` the revival's: it is the team's file, with helpers that the revival added.

## What changed and why

The first half, review-queue item 355's option 1 (`explorations/coordinator/review-queue.md:1263`):

- `stringOps` gains `getProperty(String, String): String` and `getEnvironment(String, String): String`, right after `lineSeparator`, each computing as `systemOps`' did (`stringOps.java:80-89`; `systemOps.java:20-27` at the base). `ProjectProperties` is named in full in the body, as `asExprString` names `Unprinter` (`stringOps.java:48-50`), so the edit is the two helpers only.
- `System`'s two strings name them (`Library/System.fss:39`, `:49`).
- `systemOps` loses `getEnvironment`; it keeps `getProperty` and `getArgs`, which the compiler's `CompilerSystem` imports (`Library/CompilerSystem.fss:13-14`), and the prelude is not changed before it is deleted (P-37; fork S1, `CLIMB-BATCH-28.md:438`).
- The compiled guard's two bindings name `stringOps` (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NativeHelperFamilyStringCompiled.fss:16-17`).

The second half, Q3's option 1 (P-170):

- `args : ImmutableArray[\String,ZZ32\] = immutableArray[\String\](programArgCount()).tabulate(fn (i:ZZ32): String => programArg(i))` (`Library/System.fss:29-30`), over `private programArgCount(): ZZ32` on `programArgs.count` and `private programArg(i: ZZ32): String` on `programArgs.at` (`:32-33`). `getProgramArgsPrim`, the glue binding, and `getProgramArgs`, its converter, are deleted. `System.fsi` declares only `args` (`Library/System.fsi:28`) and does not change.
- `nativeHelpers/programArgs.java`, new: `public static int count()` and `public static String at(int i)` over `MainWrapper.cachedArgs` (`programArgs.java:9-17`).
- `StringPrim.GetProgramArgs.registerProgramArgs`, which walk's driver calls before every run (`interpreter/Driver.java:546`, `:564`), sets `MainWrapper.cachedArgs` from the list it already holds, one line (`StringPrim.java:124`). The compiled main sets it before the program's `main` runs (`MainWrapper.java:67`, unchanged).

The glue class `StringPrim.GetProgramArgs` stays whole: no binding names it now, and its `registerProgramArgs` is the driver's entry.

### The static, and the loader

Fork S3 put a static `String[]` in `programArgs`, set by both drivers. Built so, with `MainWrapper.java:67` setting `programArgs.args = subargs`, the compiled path did not see the arguments:

    $ cd tmp/rung-system-natives/probe && ../../../bin/fortress compile ProgramArgsProbe.fss && ../../../bin/fortress run ProgramArgsProbe a b
    count =  0
    rc=0

The instantiating class loader loads every class itself except those that `mustUseSystemLoader` leaves to its parent (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/InstantiatingClassloader.java:2897-2919`): `MainWrapper` is on that list (`:2907`) and no class of `nativeHelpers/` is, so the program's `programArgs` was the loader's own copy, and `MainWrapper`, loaded by the system loader, wrote the other copy's field. The team's own helper over the arguments, `systemOps.getArgs`, reads `MainWrapper.cachedArgs` for this reason (`systemOps.java:24-26`). With `programArgs` reading `MainWrapper.cachedArgs`, the same probe, on the final code `ee14222d`:

    count =  2
    at(0) =  a
    at(1) =  b
    rc=0

and with no argument, `count =  0`, rc 0. Under walk a helper class is the application loader's (`Class.forName`, `interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java:175`), as are `StringPrim` and `MainWrapper`, so walk's write and read meet. A consequence: walk now initialises `MainWrapper`, and with it the instantiating loader's singleton (`MainWrapper.java:19`), in its main thread at `registerProgramArgs`; on the base it initialised neither, and it no longer initialises `systemOps` (`JAVA_FLAGS="... -Xlog:class+init=info" bin/fortress ProjectFortress/tests/SystemArgsWalk.fss`, then grep for the class names; the same on the old code):

    new: Initializing 'com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/MainWrapper' ... by thread "main"
    new: Initializing 'com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/InstantiatingClassloader' ... by thread "main"
    new: Initializing 'com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/programArgs'(no method) ... by thread "ForkJoinPool-1-worker-1"
    old: Initializing 'com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/systemOps'(no method) ... by thread "ForkJoinPool-1-worker-1"

The loader's constructor sets a system property and refuses a second loader (`InstantiatingClassloader.java:118-125`); one JVM still makes one, as a compile's JVM does. `ant testSystem` and `ant testQuick` pass on this code (below).

## The tests, the failing runs and the passing runs

The tests:

- `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NativeHelperFamilyStringCompiled.fss:16-17`, the compiled guard, retargeted onto `stringOps`.
- `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NativeHelperProgramArgsCompiled.fss` and `.test`, new: binds `programArgs.count` and `at` in its own declarations and asserts the count 0 for a run without arguments.
- `ProjectFortress/tests/SystemArgsWalk.fss`, new: prints `|args|` and each element, and asserts `|args|` is 0, as the harness passes no argument. A guard: it passes on the base and after.

The failing run, on the base's code, before the edit was first built (`ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh base ProjectFortress/compiler_tests NativeHelperFamilyStringCompiled.test NativeHelperProgramArgsCompiled.test`, 2026-11-08T05:29:51Z, tree 157323e5 with the tests applied):

The walk guard on the base (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh $PWD/tmp/rung-system-natives/h-base ProjectFortress/tests/SystemArgsWalk.fss`, 2026-11-08T05:30:08Z, tree 157323e5): `|args| = 0`, `OK (1 test)`.

## The checker over System

The planner's command (section 5, probe 3), with `-Djava.io.tmpdir` added, on the final code `ee14222d`:

    SCR=$PWD/tmp/sys-check; mkdir -p $SCR/classes $SCR/caches

## The count stage and the distance stage

Both ran once on the final code, commit `ee14222d`, with nothing uncommitted (`git status --short` printed nothing), after its build; no code changed after either started.

- The count (`explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh tmp/rung-system-natives/checker-count-postedit.txt tmp/rung-system-natives/cc-post`): `#total 0`, `#locations 0`, `#crash none`, `#shadow matches the tracked StaticChecker`. `diff explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-27/gate/checker-count.txt tmp/rung-system-natives/checker-count-postedit.txt` prints nothing.

No file's recorded first error in the baseline names what the change touched (`awk` over `explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/ladder.tsv`'s first-error column for `stringOps`, `systemOps`, `CompilerSystem`, `StringVector`, `getProgramArgs`, `getEnvironment`, `getProperty`, `MainWrapper` and `args` finds only two unrelated rows, `NatReflectTest.fss` and `XXXvarargsObject.fss`), and no program of the pass list imports `System` or `CompilerSystem`. ## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

The map's table of what moves with what (`explorations/coordinator/map/README.md:125`) and section B.12 (`map/modules-and-phases.md:441-462`) put a binding's helper in `nativeHelpers/`, read whole by the checker and the wrapper generator. `library.md`, "Designing a change": a native is a public static method of a class under `nativeHelpers/`, bound by `builtinPrimitive`. For the arguments, the team's precedent is `systemOps.getArgs` over `MainWrapper.cachedArgs` (`systemOps.java:24-26`), with `MainWrapper` delegated to the system loader (`InstantiatingClassloader.java:2907`). For an immutable array of a size known at run time the library writes `immutableArray[\T\](n)` (`Library/CovariantCollection.fss:89`, `Library/PureList.fss:133`) and fills it with `init` or `tabulate` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2576`).

The ways the language and the library offer, and the choice, are in "Decisions".

## What the specification settles

Nothing: the specification declares no api `System` (the greps in the provenance lines). The decisions are item 355's option 1, P-37, P-58 and P-170.

## Names

`grep -rn` over `ProjectFortress/tests`, `ProjectFortress/*_tests`, `ProjectFortress/test_library`, `Library`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin`, `ProjectFortress/demos` and `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress` finds `programArgCount` and `programArg` only in `Library/System.fss:32-33`; the class `programArgs` only in its file, `System.fss` and the new compiled test; `stringOps.getProperty` and `stringOps.getEnvironment` only in `System.fss` and the compiled guard; `argCount` and `argAt` only in the new compiled test; no other `SystemArgsWalk` or `NativeHelperProgramArgsCompiled`; and no use left of `getProgramArgsPrim` or `getProgramArgs`.

## Sentences made false

- `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:4625`, the natives entry's Effect: "341 of the 443 bindings of \library\ name a helper"; on this tree alone 343 of 444 (a counter over `Library/*.fss` and `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/*.fss`, the `Compiler` files left out and comments struck, which gives 341 of 443 and 102 at the base); and its list gains `System`'s two helpers of `args`, the number of arguments and the i-th argument. `:4655`: "The other 102 still name a glue class", 101 here. result.ruling:
Fix c00f51c2 (FileWriteStream's write(x:String) changed from x.writeOn(self) to under.write(x)) is UPHELD. The specification is silent: it names no I/O object, and its only sentence on interleaving is Specification/basic/evaluation/parallelism.tex:90, which is about scheduling. The library's own api settles the point. File.fsi:111-116 says writes' append "is done monolithically" to avoid interleaving, and print and println work "much like writes" (:119, :122-124). writes reaches write(x:String) whenever its joined string is not flat (Library/File.fss:59-65). The leaf-by-leaf writeOn (Library/String.fss:163-166, :493-505) breaks that promise. WriteStream says the same at Library/Stream.fss:49-54 and :64-69. The library's way is to write a rope once. The team's Writer wrapped a rope in a BufferedWriter of size |s| and flushed it, so the rope went out in one write (git show c2178040^:Library/Writer.fss, lines 45-49; the glue buffer is at interpreter/glue/prim/BufferedWriter.java:34-38). Rung W flattens and writes once (Library/Writer.fss:31-35), for the reason in rung-io-writer/REPORT.md:144, decision 7. The team's ConcurrentPrinting.fss states the intent. Fork R2's default also says "its writes, flush and close over under, as Writer's are" (CLIMB-BATCH-28.md:406).

Worker, right: rows 900 and 901 need only WriteStream and flush. The team's FileWriteStream flushes in none of its writes, and the fix keeps that buffering.
Worker, wrong: "the team's text already writes a rope through writeOn" is no evidence. That text never ran on the base, where a rope stopped the run (row 900, REPORT.md:59). Also wrong: reading fork R2 as covering only the primitive writes ignores its "as Writer's are".

Skeptic, right: the measured broken lines ('432 =/= ... 600' and '252 =/= ... 600' through harness-one.sh at four threads on 9632f4e5, then 'OK (8 tests)' after the fix); File.fsi's text; fork R2's words; rung W's decision 7; and that the base could never break a line.
Skeptic, partly right: "as Writer's are" also covers Writer's flush after a rope (Library/Writer.fss:34), which the fix leaves out. File.fsi asks no write to flush (:102-109, :127-128), and the single write is enough for a monolithic append, so the fix stands as it is. The divergence goes to the curator. The write is atomic because it is one call to java.io.BufferedWriter.write (compiler/runtimeValues/FortressBufferedWriter.java:47-50, via fileOps.java:109-111).

rulings.why: File.fsi:111-116 promises writes' append is monolithic; the team's Writer (c2178040^:Library/Writer.fss:45-49) and rung W's Writer (Library/Writer.fss:31-35, rung-io-writer/REPORT.md:144) write a rope once; fork R2 says 'as Writer's are' (CLIMB-BATCH-28.md:406). Broken lines were measured at 432 and 252 of 600 on 9632f4e5, and the rung's repair of row 900 made them reachable. The fix keeps the worker's buffering by adding no flush.

forCurator: FileWriteStream's write of a string that is not flat makes one write and no flush (Library/File.fss:57). Writer's flushes after it (Library/Writer.fss:32-35), and fork R2's default says 'as Writer's are' (explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-28.md:406). Option 1, as landed: no flush. This keeps the file stream's buffering, so its other writes behave as before (Library/File.fss:54-55, :67-68). Option 2: add a flush after it, as Writer does and as the team's Writer did (git show c2178040^:Library/Writer.fss, line 48). That is one line, and a rope's write would then flush where a flat string's does not. Lines stay whole either way.
result.summary: I upheld the one contested fix, c00f51c2, so rung R lands as wip/rung-io-reader holds it: no revert and no repair round. The fix makes FileWriteStream's write(x:String) a single under.write(x), so lines that parallel tasks write to one file stay whole. The specification says nothing on this. The library's api does: File.fsi:111-116 promises a monolithic append. The team's Writer and rung W's Writer both write a rope once, and fork R2 says "as Writer's are". Through the harness at four threads, the skeptic's test FileWriteStreamParallelWalk failed at 432 and 252 of 600 on 9632f4e5 and passed after the fix. The worker was right that rows 900 and 901 need only WriteStream and flush, and that the stream should keep its buffering; the fix keeps it. The worker was wrong to cite the team's x.writeOn(self), which never ran on the base. One divergence goes to the curator: the fix adds no flush, where Writer flushes after a rope. Lines 17, 149 and 198 of REPORT.md still describe 9632f4e5; JUDGE.md tells the gather so. The ruling is /home/user/fortress-io-reader/explorations/compile-ladder/rung-io-reader/JUDGE.md, committed as a7486729 and pushed.
